concept.name: CI/CD Quality Gates

relationships.description: Connects CI/CD Quality Gates to canary deployments in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: CI/CD quality gates are automated, deterministic checkpoints—spanning unit/contract tests, SAST/SCA security scans, policy-as-code, and canary SLO analysis—that block defective or vulnerable artifacts from advancing toward production.
spark.keyTakeaway: Design quality gates as a fast-to-slow funnel: fail bad commits in <3 minutes with linting, unit tests, and SAST, reserve heavy integration/load suites for merge queues, and enforce automated canary metric rollbacks in production.

concept.whyItMatters: Shipping 50+ times a day without automated guardrails simply accelerates how fast bugs, leaked secrets, and vulnerable dependencies reach production. Manual QA sign-offs and CAB (Change Advisory Board) meetings create week-long bottlenecks without catching subtle concurrency bugs or supply-chain CVEs. Automated CI/CD quality gates shift verification left into seconds-fast PR feedback while enforcing non-negotiable security, contract, and SLO standards at every promotion boundary.
whenToUse: On every Pull Request and main-branch merge to block regressions, critical CVEs, leaked credentials, and breaking API schema changes before artifacts are published.
At staging/pre-prod promotion boundaries to validate database migrations, OpenAPI/Pact consumer contracts, and P99 latency under synthetic load.
During progressive production rollouts (canary/blue-green) using automated metric gates (Argo Rollouts / Flagger) to halt bad releases within minutes.
whenNotToUse: Do not put flaky, 30-minute end-to-end browser tests on the blocking PR fast-path—they destroy developer velocity and train engineers to blindly click 'Re-run'.
Do not enforce arbitrary 95% line-coverage rules on boilerplate DTOs or glue code, which incentivizes meaningless assertion-free tests.
For emergency break-glass hotfixes during a Sev-1 outage, ensure a documented, audited bypass path exists rather than forcing responders to wait on a 25-minute non-critical scan.
keyPoints: Stage gates by feedback speed (the **Testing Trophy**): fast static checks, SAST, and unit tests run in <3 minutes on PRs; contract and integration tests run on merge queues; heavy E2E and soak tests run post-merge or pre-canary.

**Policy-as-Code** (OPA/Conftest, Kyverno) enforces infrastructure invariants—such as blocking public S3 buckets, missing Kubernetes `resources.limits`, or `:latest` container tags—deterministically in CI.
**Supply-chain gates** (Trivy, Grype, Semgrep, Gitleaks, Sigstore Cosign) block critical/high CVEs with available fixes, secret leaks, and unsigned container images before deployment.
**Contract testing** (Pact, Buf breaking-change checks) verifies producer/consumer compatibility independently, eliminating brittle shared-staging E2E bottlenecks.

**Automated Canary Analysis (ACA)** compares canary vs. baseline error rates, P99 latency, and saturation in production (e.g., Kayenta or Argo Rollouts `AnalysisTemplate`) and auto-rolls back without human intervention.

examples.title: Fintech Microservice Pipeline with Pact & Canary SLO Gates
examples.scenario: A payments team with 18 microservices suffered from a flaky 45-minute shared-staging E2E suite that blocked merges and still missed backward-incompatible Protobuf changes.
examples.outcome: Replacing shared-staging E2E with `buf breaking` + Pact contract gates on PRs cut PR feedback from 45 minutes to 4 minutes. Adding an Argo Rollouts canary gate (5% traffic for 10 minutes checking HTTP 5xx < 0.1% and P99 < 180 ms via Prometheus) caught 3 memory-leak regressions automatically before reaching 100% of users.

examples.title: Shift-Left Container & IaC Security Gate in GitHub Actions
examples.scenario: An audit found unencrypted RDS snapshots, overly permissive IAM wildcards, and 14 critical CVEs in production containers.
examples.outcome: The platform team added Gitleaks, Semgrep, Trivy (`--severity CRITICAL --exit-code 1 --ignore-unfixed`), and Conftest (OPA Rego policies on Terraform plans) to GitHub Actions, plus Cosign keyless signing on ECR pushes. Critical CVE drift dropped to zero and insecure Terraform PRs were blocked at review time.

tradeOffs.factor: Strict Blocking Gates vs. Advisory Warnings
tradeOffs.pro: Hard-failing builds on critical CVEs, broken contracts, or Terraform policy violations guarantees compliance and prevents known-bad deploys.
tradeOffs.con: False positives (e.g., an unpatchable CVE or a flaky test) halt all engineering delivery until triaged or explicitly exempted.

tradeOffs.factor: PR-Time Heavy E2E vs. Merge Queue + Canary Gates
tradeOffs.pro: Running full E2E on every PR catches cross-service bugs before code ever hits `main`.
tradeOffs.con: Slows PR iteration by 20–40 minutes and multiplies CI compute bills; using GitHub Merge Queues + production canary gates preserves both speed and safety.

tradeOffs.factor: Strict Coverage Thresholds vs. Mutation / Critical-Path Testing
tradeOffs.pro: Enforcing 80% coverage on new diff lines prevents completely untested business logic from landing.
tradeOffs.con: Global coverage gates encourage gaming the metric; combining diff-coverage with critical-path integration tests yields higher real defect detection.

failureModes.name: Flaky Gate Normalization
failureModes.description: A non-deterministic integration test fails 8% of runs; engineers develop 're-run fatigue' and ignore real failures or disable the gate entirely.
failureModes.mitigation: Track test flakiness rates, auto-quarantine tests failing >1% non-deterministically within 24 hours, and require deterministic Testcontainers/wiremock fixtures.

failureModes.name: Gate Bypass & Shadow Deploys
failureModes.description: Developers push hotfixes directly from laptops via `kubectl apply` or `terraform apply` when CI takes 30 minutes, bypassing all security and test gates.
failureModes.mitigation: Revoke direct prod write IAM/RBAC from human users, enforce GitOps (ArgoCD/Flux) + admission controllers (Kyverno verifying Cosign signatures), and provide a fast audited break-glass workflow.

failureModes.name: Unbounded CVE Breakage
failureModes.description: A newly published midnight CVE in a base OS package (`openssl` or `glibc`) suddenly breaks every PR across 50 repos—even when no upstream fix exists yet.
failureModes.mitigation: Configure Trivy/Grype with `--ignore-unfixed`, maintain central golden base images updated daily, and use time-boxed VEX/exception files for false positives.

failureModes.name: Noisy Canary False Rollbacks
failureModes.description: A canary gate compares 5% traffic against 95% baseline during low-traffic night hours; 2 random client timeouts trigger an unnecessary rollback.
failureModes.mitigation: Require minimum sample sizes (e.g., >=500 requests per window) and use statistical Mann-Whitney U / Kayenta comparisons rather than naive raw-percentage thresholds.

commonMistakes: Putting 20-minute Selenium/Playwright UI suites as a blocking check on every backend PR instead of using contract tests and targeted smoke suites.
Running security scans in 'report-only' mode forever—nobody reads 400-line JSON warnings unless critical findings actually fail the pipeline.
Validating only application code while ignoring Terraform, Helm, and Dockerfile misconfigurations (e.g., running containers as `root` or exposing port 22).
Treating `main` as green enough and skipping progressive delivery gates (canary/blue-green) in production, where config and scale bugs actually manifest.
Failing to pin GitHub Action versions by commit SHA or sign build artifacts, leaving the CI/CD pipeline itself vulnerable to supply-chain tampering.

sections.content:
## The idea

CI/CD quality gates are automated, non-negotiable verification checkpoints placed along the path from `git push` to 100% production traffic. Instead of relying on manual QA sign-offs or post-incident blame, quality gates encode engineering, security, and reliability standards directly into executable code.

The core design principle is **tiered latency matching**: cheap, deterministic checks (linting, unit tests, SAST, secret scanning) fail bad commits in under 3 minutes on every Pull Request; heavier cross-service checks (contract tests, Testcontainers, IaC policy validation) guard the merge queue and artifact promotion; and live **Automated Canary Analysis (ACA)** verifies real-world SLOs before full rollout.

## Concrete walkthrough

Follow a payment-service Pull Request through a production-grade 4-stage quality-gate pipeline:

1. **Stage 1 — Fast PR Gate (<3 min):** GitHub Actions runs in parallel: `gitleaks` (secret scan), `golangci-lint` / `eslint`, unit tests with >=80% diff coverage, `semgrep` SAST, and `buf breaking` to ensure no backward-incompatible gRPC/Protobuf changes.
2. **Stage 2 — Merge Queue & Artifact Gate (5–8 min):** Upon approval, the merge queue runs Pact consumer-driven contract verification and ephemeral PostgreSQL integration tests via Testcontainers. On pass, it builds a multi-arch distroless container, scans it with `trivy image --severity CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed`, generates an SBOM, and signs the digest with **Sigstore Cosign**.
3. **Stage 3 — Admission & Staging Gate:** ArgoCD syncs to staging. Kyverno verifies the Cosign signature and blocks any manifest missing `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` or CPU/memory limits. A 2-minute k6 smoke test validates P99 latency < 150 ms.
4. **Stage 4 — Production Canary Gate:** Argo Rollouts shifts 5% of live traffic to the new digest for 10 minutes. An `AnalysisTemplate` queries Prometheus every 60 seconds: if HTTP 5xx > 0.2% or P99 latency > 200 ms, Argo automatically aborts and shifts 100% traffic back to baseline.

sections.content:
## Supply-chain & policy-as-code gates

Modern quality gates go far beyond unit tests—they secure the build pipeline and infrastructure itself:

- **SLSA Provenance & Image Signing:** Use **Sigstore Cosign** (keyless OIDC) to sign container digests at build time and enforce **Kyverno** or **OPA Gatekeeper** admission rules in Kubernetes so unsigned or manually built images can never run in production.
- **Terraform / IaC Plan Gates:** Run **Conftest** (Rego) or **Checkov** against `terraform plan -out=tfplan.binary` JSON in PRs to block `0.0.0.0/0` security groups, unencrypted S3 buckets, or public RDS instances before `apply`.
- **Secret & Dependency Hygiene:** Run **Gitleaks** on commit diffs and **Trivy/Grype** with `--ignore-unfixed` so known critical CVEs are blocked without halting builds on unpatchable upstream bugs.

## Quality gate layers & SLA targets

| Gate Stage | Typical Checks | Target Duration | Failure Action | Bypass Policy |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Pre-Commit / PR Fast Gate** | Linter, Unit Tests, Semgrep SAST, Gitleaks | 1–3 minutes | Block PR merge | Never (except audited docs-only skip) |
| **Merge Queue / Artifact** | Pact Contracts, Testcontainers, Trivy CVE, Cosign | 5–10 minutes | Reject from merge queue | Time-boxed VEX exception for false-positive CVEs |
| **Cluster Admission Gate** | Kyverno/OPA signature, non-root, resource limits | <1 second | Reject Kubernetes Pod/Deployment | Break-glass cluster-admin role (audited) |
| **Production Canary Gate** | Prometheus 5xx, P99 latency, saturation (Argo/Flagger) | 10–20 minutes | Auto-abort & instant rollback to baseline | Manual promote only after incident review |

## Failure modes

- **Flaky Test Erosion:** A 5% flaky integration test causes developers to hit 'Re-run' blindly, masking genuine regressions and eroding trust in CI.
- **Slow-Gate Queue Jamming:** A 35-minute blocking E2E suite on `main` creates a 10-PR backlog, forcing teams to bundle massive risky diffs together.
- **Canary Metric Blind Spots:** Checking only HTTP 5xx in a canary gate misses silent data corruption, 4xx spikes from broken validation, or memory leaks that take 30 minutes to OOMKill.
- **Unpinned CI Dependencies:** Using `@main` or mutable `:latest` tags on third-party GitHub Actions or scanner images exposes your pipeline to supply-chain compromises.

## Measuring gate effectiveness (DORA & flakiness)

Quality gates should improve both **stability** and **velocity**—measure them continuously using DORA metrics:

- **Change Failure Rate (CFR):** Target <5% of production deployments requiring rollback or hotfix; if CFR rises, analyze escaped defects to add targeted contract or canary checks.
- **PR Feedback Time:** Keep Stage 1 under 5 minutes and total merge-to-prod under 25 minutes by parallelizing matrix jobs and caching build layers.
- **Flake Rate SLO:** Enforce a <0.5% non-deterministic failure rate across all blocking CI jobs; automatically quarantine and file a P1 bug on any test that flakes twice in a week.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Split CI into a <3-minute PR fast gate (lint, unit, SAST, secret scan) and a merge-queue/post-merge gate for heavier integration tests.
- [ ] Replace brittle shared-staging E2E suites with Pact consumer-driven contracts and `buf`/OpenAPI breaking-change checks.
- [ ] Scan container images (`trivy --ignore-unfixed`) and Terraform plans (OPA/Conftest) as hard-blocking checks, and sign production images with Cosign.
- [ ] Enforce GitOps + Kubernetes admission policies (Kyverno/OPA) so no human can `kubectl apply` unverified artifacts to production.
- [ ] Wire Argo Rollouts or Flagger canary gates to Prometheus golden signals with minimum sample-size thresholds and automatic rollback.

interviewProblems.title: CI/CD Quality Gates
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on CI/CD Quality Gates. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: CI/CD quality gates are automated, deterministic checkpoints—spanning unit/contract tests, SAST/SCA security scans, policy-as-code, and canary SLO analysis—that block defective or vulnerable artifacts from advancing toward production.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Policy & Admission applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Canary SLO Gate.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Canary SLO Gate experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Track test flakiness rates, auto-quarantine tests failing >1% non-deterministically within 24 hours, and require deterministic Testcontainers/wiremock fixtures.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Design quality gates as a fast-to-slow funnel: fail bad commits in <3 minutes with linting, unit tests, and SAST, reserve heavy integration/load suites for merge queues, and enforce automated canary metric rollbacks in production.
Avoid trap: Putting 20-minute Selenium/Playwright UI suites as a blocking check on every backend PR instead of using contract tests and targeted smoke suites.
Avoid trap: Running security scans in 'report-only' mode forever—nobody reads 400-line JSON warnings unless critical findings actually fail the pipeline.
When to reach for it: On every Pull Request and main-branch merge to block regressions, critical CVEs, leaked credentials, and breaking API schema changes before artifacts are published.
When to reach for it: At staging/pre-prod promotion boundaries to validate database migrations, OpenAPI/Pact consumer contracts, and P99 latency under synthetic load.

putItTogether.title: Putting Cicd Quality Gates Together
putItTogether.summary: Design quality gates as a fast-to-slow funnel: fail bad commits in <3 minutes with linting, unit tests, and SAST, reserve heavy integration/load suites for merge queues, and enforce automated canary metric rollbacks in production.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Cicd Quality Gates before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Replacing shared-staging E2E with `buf breaking` + Pact contract gates on PRs cut PR feedback from 45 minutes to 4 minutes. Adding an Argo Rollouts canary gate (5% traffic for 10 minutes checking HTTP 5xx < 0.1% and P99 < 180 ms via Prometheus) caught 3 memory-leak regressions automatically before reaching 100% of users.
